_README: One rider_id that is really two people, and which of its results belong to the second. The MIRROR of rider_aliases.json in the other direction: aliases fuse ids, this fissions one. CONSULTED AT INGEST for the same reason aliases are — link_gravel_riders.py keys riders on the folded NAME, so two people called Tom Miller collapse to one id every time it runs, and a split applied only to the database is undone by the next rebuild. A rule therefore keys on something the scrape file actually carries: the race and the year. Rows that match no rule stay on the original id, so adding a rider here can only ever move the rows it names. A split is a claim exactly as strong as a merge and fractures one career if it is wrong, so the bar used here is a contradiction inside a single id that is too large to be Athlinks age noise — which this archive measures at plus or minus 3 to 5 years. Two candidates were REJECTED at that bar and are listed at the bottom so nobody re-derives them.

rider/tom-miller.evidence: This id holds Chequamegon 2003, 2006 and 2007 plus Unbound 2015. Its own rows make one person impossible: age 26 at Chequamegon 2007 and age 46 at Unbound 2015 is twenty years of ageing across eight calendar years. The Chequamegon rows agree with each other — age 25 in 2006 and 26 in 2007 both give 1981 — so it is the Unbound row that belongs to somebody else, a Tom Miller born about 1969. Different race, different state, and a gap four times the noise floor.

rider/mark-smith.evidence: This id holds Leadville 1994, 2008, 2010 and 2011. Age 42 in 1994 and age 49 in 2008 is seven years of ageing across fourteen calendar years; a rider born 1952 would have been 56 in 2008. The later rows agree with each other — 49 in 2008 and 50 in 2011 give 1959 and 1961 — so the 1994 ride belongs to an older Mark Smith, born about 1952. rider/mark-p-smith, Leadville 1998 at age 39, implies 1959 and therefore belongs with the LATER group, which is why it stays on the original id.

rejected.rider/paul-ellis: NOT split. Proposed as a conflation on 2026-09-12 and that was an over-call, corrected the same day. Its implied birth years run 1981, 1980, 1980, 1984 — a spread of 4, which IS the Athlinks noise floor, not evidence of two people. Its worst single contradiction is age 28 in 2008 followed by age 25 in 2009, three years in one, ordinary noise. The thing that made it look conflated was social, not numerical: it had already absorbed a paul-L-ellis and a later sweep offered it a paul-C-ellis. Two middle initials is a reason to leave paul-c-ellis unmerged, which it is, and not a reason to fission what is here.
rejected.rider/jake-pantone: NOT split, despite carrying THREE Athlinks racer ids — 176052831 (Leadville 2011), 333542089 (Unbound 2018) and 165673321 (Unbound 2019 and 2021). Surfaced 2026-09-18 by audit_rider_racer_ids.py's mirror section, which reports several racer ids on one of our ids as the shape a conflation would have, and checked the same day. It is one man with three registrations. The decisive evidence is the birth year: ages 30, 37, 38 and 40 in 2011, 2018, 2019 and 2021 imply 1981 EVERY TIME, with zero variance across a ten-year span — a conflation of two people cannot normally hold that, and this archive's own noise floor is plus or minus 3 to 5 years. The localities agree too: Eden on three rows and Huntsville on the fourth are two of the three communities of Ogden Valley, Weber County, Utah, and the 'CO' region beside Huntsville is LEADVILLE's state, the documented region artefact, not a move to Colorado. The id never appears twice in one edition. SEPARATELY, rider/ike-pantone is NOT this man and must never be merged into him: Ike rode Unbound 2021 in 50th at 46,807s while Jake rode the same edition in 42nd at 45,855s, so they share a stage, which is the test that proves two people. Ike is Ogden, born 1985 — twelve miles down the canyon and almost certainly a relative. audit_rider_duplicates.py does not currently pair the two names, so there is no `separated` entry; this note is the record.
rejected.rider/aaron-campbell: NOT split, and the six-year birth-year spread is the reason it LOOKS split rather than evidence that it is. Racer 397998872 carries BOTH ends of that spread by itself — age 30 at Leadville 2012 implying 1982 and age 38 at Leadville 2014 implying 1976 — so the contradiction sits inside one Athlinks account and cannot be a second person. The third row, Leadville 2013 on racer 149233254, agrees with 2014 on 1976. Farmington and Kaysville are neighbouring Davis County, Utah towns, and the 'CO' beside Farmington in 2012 is LEADVILLE's state, the documented region artefact. His results improve 88th, 45th, 14th over the three years. Checked 2026-09-18.
rejected.rider/alex-wild: NOT split. 18 rows, 2018-2025, ages running 26 to 33 without a contradiction, and Los Gatos then San Jose are both Santa Clara County, California. The binding detail is bib 73 across FIVE different 2024 races — Big Sugar, Chequamegon, Leadville, Sea Otter and Unbound — which is one rider carrying one Life Time Grand Prix number. Racer 330254832 appears only in 2018 and 498697090 from 2021, an old account replaced by a newer one. Checked 2026-09-18.
rejected.rider/elliot-bach: NOT split, on thinner evidence than the others here, recorded so the thinness itself is not re-derived. Only two rows — Unbound 2021 (racer 399789618, no age, no locality) and Leadville 2022 (racer 99968247, age 29, Boulder, Colorado) — so just one row carries an age and nothing can contradict anything. What there is points one way: 'Bach' is a surname of exactly two riders in the whole archive and the other is a French road rider filed as 'Bach Constant'. No contradiction, a rare name, and no shared stage. Revisit if a third row ever disagrees. Checked 2026-09-18.
rejected.rider/mark-currie: NOT split. Both dated rows give 1995 — age 20 at Leadville 2015 and age 26 at Unbound 2021 — and the locality change from Ogden, Utah to Longmont, Colorado is a move, which is also exactly when the second racer id (390196398) replaces the first (325071199). The 'CO' beside Ogden in 2015 is Leadville's state, not his. Checked 2026-09-18.
rejected.rider/mark-walker: NOT split. All six rows imply 1974 and every row that carries a locality reads Salida, Colorado. Four of the six carry no racer id at all; the two that do are consecutive years, 338838348 in 2018 and 370693392 in 2019, which is a re-registration rather than a second man. The 'KS' on the 2010 row with no locality is UNBOUND's own state. Checked 2026-09-18.
rejected.rider/matt-acker: NOT split. Seven rows, every one located Grand Rapids, Michigan (twice in capitals, which is the entrant's own typing), implying 1985 or 1986 throughout. The second racer id, 304711553, appears on a single 2015 Unbound row; 125446627 carries the other five that have one. The two 2023 rows disagree with each other by a year, 38 and 37 in the same season, which is the ordinary Athlinks age noise. Checked 2026-09-18.
rejected.rider/matti-rowe: NOT split. Four Unbound rows 2021-2025, all implying 1987, all located Longmont, Colorado. Racer 498694765 in 2021 and 525148609 from 2023, with 2025 carrying none. Checked 2026-09-18.
rejected.rider/nathan-keck: NOT split, and the two localities are the same town written two ways: '57783, SD' at Leadville 2015 is the ZIP code for Spearfish, South Dakota, which is what the 2018 and 2019 Unbound rows spell out. Ages 30, 32 and 33 imply 1985, 1986, 1986. 'Keck' belongs to two riders in the whole archive and the other is not a candidate. Note this id has already absorbed rider/nathan-keck-sram, a sponsor glued to the name at Leadville 2015. Checked 2026-09-18.
rejected.rider/ryan-petry: NOT split, and the two racer ids are the clue rather than the problem: 84638762 and 84638767 are FIVE APART, which is one person registering twice in one sitting, not two men. Ages imply 1991 or 1992 across all six rows, and Birmingham, Michigan to Boulder, Colorado is a move — the 2012 row's 'CO' region is Leadville's state while the town is still Birmingham. Leadville's own seeding binds the early rows: 11th in 2014 and bib 11 in 2015, an exact hit. Checked 2026-09-18.
rejected.rider/sam-benedict: EXAMINED 2026-09-18 and DELIBERATELY NOT DECIDED. This entry is a record that the question was looked at and the evidence does not reach a verdict — it is NOT a ruling that the two racer ids are one person, and nobody should read it as one. Only two rows exist: Leadville 2017 (racer 302976180, bib 13, no age, no locality) and Leadville 2018 (racer 343367626, bib 791, age 34, Gilroy, California). One age between them, so nothing can contradict anything. The seeding argument does not work here either: bib 13 then bib 791 would break Leadville's rule that a returning rider gets last year's finish, but our 2017 field is 18 rows whose ranks are not even time-ordered — rank 14 finishes in 10.47h and rank 15 in 6.54h — so that 'rank 14' is not a real 14th place and cannot seed anything. The blocker is OUR Leadville coverage for 2016-2018, not the riders; see the coverage note in ai-context.md. What would settle it: a fuller 2016-2018 Leadville field, or any third row for either id.
rejected.rider/mike-johnson: NOT split. Its worst contradiction is age 32 in 2007 against age 41 in 2010 — nine years in three, a gap of 6, which sits at the edge of the noise floor rather than beyond it. The supporting argument was that its 2007 row carries bib 948 where its others carry 48 to 229, an unseeded bib among seeded ones; that argument does not survive checking. Chequamegon 2007 bibs run to 1867 and 56 of the 98 rows this archive stores for that edition carry a bib of 800 or more, with a median finish of 63rd. Bib 948 finishing 67th is the most ordinary row in the field. Mike Johnson is also the commonest name in the off-road set, so a second one is entirely possible — there is just no evidence here that reaches the bar.
